newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India awards two diesel cargoes in 2nd Jan tender.
newsitem.headline: India awards two diesel cargoes in 2nd Jan tender.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) bought 90,000 tonnes of high speed diesel in two cargoes in its second tender for January delivery, traders said on Monday.

The first cargo of 0.5-percent sulphur diesel was awarded to European major Shell at a premium of $25.88 per barrel to the high of Mediterranean spot quotes, for January 16-23 delivery on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to Kandla on the Indian west coast.
The second cargo was awarded to German trader Stinnes at a premium of $25.85 per barrel to the high of Mediterranean quotes for January 24-31 delivery, c-and-f Kandla.
The tender closed on December 11 and was valid until December 13.
Traders said India's decision to award Mediterranean-based cargoes reflected the more competitive prices seen there compared with MidEast cargoes.
This might also reflect the possibility of the arbitrage being more accessible from the Mediterranean, they added.
For the past several months, IOC had only awarded cargoes which were MidEast-based since Mediterranean-based cargoes have been too expensive, reflecting the tightness of the market there.
In its first tender for January, IOC awarded 255,000 tonnes of diesel in six cargoes, which were all priced on MidEast spot quotes.
